title: demand.json _comment corrupted by botched text splice: 'USER RULING 20the shipped app starts at Foundations'
evidence: +  "_comment": "Demand catalog ... the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 20the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 2026-08-28) and advances via the 6.2 gate; the era-3 plans fire when the run reaches the Streaming Surge.",
detail: The comment edit spliced a replacement mid-token, duplicating 'the shipped app starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 20...' inside itself. Still valid JSON, but the catalog file now carries visibly corrupted provenance text.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the _comment cleanly: single occurrence of the ruling sentence, e.g. '...starts at Foundations (era 1, USER RULING 2026-08-28) and advances via the 6.2 gate; era-3 plans fire at the Streaming Surge.'

title: New econ unit test fails open: catalog-load failure prints to stderr and returns, test passes green
detail: The file's stated purpose is 'a silent episode-free era-2 run can never ship green again', yet a broken catalog environment yields a silently green row. The gate is vacuous precisely when its setup regresses.
recommended_fix: Replace the print-and-return with t.failf("econ unit: catalog load failed: %s", e) (or testing.errorf) so setup failure fails the test instead of skipping it.

title: Tautological sanity assertion: stats.crises >= 0 can never fail
detail: crises is an i32 only ever incremented (stats.crises += 1), so >= 0 is always true. In a test whose header boasts it pins the 'VACUITY premise', this line is itself dead coverage.
recommended_fix: Delete the line, or make it meaningful (e.g. assert the expected deterministic crisis count for seed 42, or crises >= 1 if the era-2 brush must trigger).

title: Retained if cerr.file != "balance.json" guard is now redundant after the unconditional assertion
detail: The new unconditional expect already flags any non-balance.json file; the guard below re-tests the same condition and can only execute after a recorded failure. Harmless, but duplicated logic left behind by the hardening.
recommended_fix: Drop the redundant if/return block (the rule-contains check is safe to run unconditionally now), or comment why the early return is kept.

title: crises_resolved field and its writer removed; readers not visible in diff
evidence:
-	crises_resolved: i32, // internal: Crisis_Resolved events seen
...
-			if e.tag == pp.EVENT_TAG_CRISIS_RESOLVED do stats.crises_resolved += 1
detail: The struct field and its only visible writer are deleted. If any elided code (e.g. econ_check gate logic between the shown hunks) read crises_resolved, the build breaks. Compile verification must confirm removal is complete.
recommended_fix: Build the harness verb; if clean, removal is complete. Consider noting in the commit message that Crisis_Resolved tracking was intentionally dropped in favor of the trigger latch.

title: PP_DEBUG start-era assertions are compiled out of default builds; nothing shows CI ever runs a PP_DEBUG build
evidence:
+	when #config(PP_DEBUG, false) {
+		testing.expectf(t, app_start_era() == APP_ERA, "the PP_DEBUG override must pin the streaming-surge start (got %d)", app_start_era())
detail: Odin's when is compile-time: in a default-config CI run the streaming-surge branch does not exist, so the r4 B5 override leg ('==1 must not fire under PP_DEBUG') is never exercised unless some job builds with PP_DEBUG. Not proven absent from the diff alone.
recommended_fix: Ensure CI (or a harness verb) also builds/tests with -define:PP_DEBUG=true so the override branch actually runs; otherwise the debug-path guarantee stays manual.

title: dots_during_crisis increment precedes the new trigger latch in the same loop — latch may be too late for the trigger tick
detail: The increment appears earlier in the loop body than the latch. If its (elided) guard reads saw_crisis_active, the trigger-tick dot the fix targets is still missed; it works only if the guard reads crisis.active state directly.
recommended_fix: Verify the increment's guard: if it tests saw_crisis_active, hoist the latch (or reorder) so the trigger tick itself is counted, and add a seed-fixed regression asserting dots@crisis > 0 on a trigger-tick dot.
